source_note: the reference shows no rabbit: it is only the yard's tilled field and grass whose palette and evening light the rabbit must match; draw one rabbit and nothing else, no field, no fences, no figures
design: small wild brown rabbit with a soft grey-brown coat, a paler buff belly and chest, a white fluffy tail, long upright ears with dark tips, large dark eyes, a pink-brown nose, short front legs and long hind feet
view_pose: Whole animal from the tips of its ears down to its paws, sitting up on all four paws in a neutral alert pose, head level, ears upright, nothing cropped; the spine points exactly along the view direction, so in a front or back view the body is foreshortened straight behind the head with the two front legs side by side and symmetric, not turned three-quarter, and in a profile view the spine runs exactly sideways
gait: Quick rabbit hop on the spot, two hops a second: the long hind feet push off together and the front paws land first, ears upright, back arching and stretching with each hop; its body never moves forward
attack: lowers its head to nibble the grass right at its front paws, nose twitching, then sits back up to the start pose; all four paws stay on the same spot
death: startles and drops: its legs give way and it sinks down onto its belly and then onto its side on the exact spot where it sat, ears flat on the ground; it never leaps or springs

turntable.design: small wild brown rabbit with a soft grey-brown coat, a paler buff belly and chest, a white fluffy tail, long upright ears with dark tips, large dark eyes, a pink-brown nose, short front legs and long hind feet, sitting on all four paws

view_notes.S: Seen exactly from the front, not three-quarter like a rabbit sitting side-on: like looking at a rabbit hopping straight at you, its head points straight at the camera with both of its eyes and both ears equally visible, and the face, neck and chest are square and symmetric about the image's vertical centre line. Only the front of the face, the throat and the chest show; the body is completely hidden straight behind the chest. The two front paws stand side by side, symmetric, and the two hind feet only just peek out behind them
